key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence reveals that PEABF4 treatment initially passivates the ETL/perovskite interface but accelerates degradation under thermal aging, with recombination losses extending into the absorber.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive, nondestructive monitoring can help engineers distinguish initial interface-passivation benefits from long-term thermal-stability penalties in perovskite solar-cell stacks.
method: Use multiple excitation wavelengths to probe depth-dependent photoluminescence responses.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret PL decay signatures using diffusion-recombination simulations.
evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced fullerene-deposition-induced interfacial losses before aging and faster degradation afterward, while simulations support interpretations involving surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
watch_item: Depth assignments are model-supported rather than direct spatial measurements, and the abstract provides no quantitative degradation rates or device-lifetime validation.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
